The engine is called Duality. I've found it while browsing the GitHub projects page. It was featured in there, and it got my attention.

It is a 2D game development framework, based (or powered) by C#. Currently, it supports Windows only. But in the near future, cross-platform may be possible.

Features

  • Plugin Architecture: Easily introduce game logic via plugins
  • Component Based Design: Allows your own code to blend in seamlessly
  • Base Infrastructure: Rendering, Audio, Physics, User Input, ...
  • Content Management: Takes care of all your game resources
  • Live Editing: Preview and Test directly in the editor
  • Hot-Reload Resources: Modified Assets are automatically reloaded
  • Hot-Reload Plugins: Write code and test it directly without restart
  • Modular Design: Tailor the editor exactly to fit your game

What makes it different from the other 2D engines?

Here's a comparison made by SirePi, a member of the Duality community:

  • Starting from scratch: you have an empty plot of land, there is a forest, some stone, and you have a few tools.
  • Low level frameworks (XNA, SFML, ...): you have some premade panels that you can arrange how you want to make a room, a forest, stone, some pre-cut lumber and materials, and some machines that help you do the work.
  • Duality: you have a room that you can stretch and reshape how you want, walls are already painted and the floor is down, but you can still paint over them or change the tiles. You have unlimited access to IKEA and to the woodshop if you so prefer. Lots of machines.
  • Others (Unity, ...): you can choose the room and furniture you want from a shiny catalogue, but the instructions on how to make your own are written in an obscure and forgotten language.

To create in TorBrowser:

  1. Click on Tools->BookMarks->View Bookmarks Toolbar.
  2. Right click on the Toolbar, select New Bookmark
  3. In New Bookmark window, Create a name for the Bookmark i.e. "Auto-downvote"
  4. Under Location, paste the script from the pastebin account
  5. Press Add, your link will appear in the toolbar
  6. Go to comments section you want to mass downvote
  7. Run bookmark you just created, all comments will be downvoted

Don't use this on user profiles, it might appear to work but I don't think profile downvotes are actually registered.

Have fun!

Even though voting calculations are queued the votes still represent a logged HTTP request at the time of receipt. Yes TOR will introduce some timing irregularities but probably not enough to make this look organic.

Voting is already periodic based on how people read a page. Give me some pseudocode for how you'd detect such voting from server side as opposed to normal use.

I suspect they're more interested in measuring queue adjacency (general flood detection) and that's how they detect brigading. I've used this script before they started hiding up/down votes. It worked mostly fine, though some votes were not registered on a refresh. From my own testing, I've had an account shadowbanned for simply rapidly pressing the up vote on a single comment.

If you're really concerned about it, the script operates in real time so you could scroll down the page and upvote a few posts while it's running.

EDIT Most importantly, I doubt their algorithm is very sophisticated considering the fact that users have had to regularly report to the admins suspected brigade activity so they could manually investigate - in which case, you're probably going to not worry much about a burner account being banned.
